comments.item_title: Apartment Rent Ordinance amendment: annual rent-increase cap
comments.subject: Opposition to lowering the rent cap
comments.text: I own a small fourplex in the Burbank area that I inherited. I OPPOSE lowering the rent cap. My insurance, water, and maintenance costs rise faster than the allowed increase already. Tightening it will force small owners to sell to big corporations. Regulate the mega-landlords, not the mom-and-pops. Vote no.

Please find attached the formal position letter of the Silicon Valley Apartment Owners Association. Our association OPPOSES lowering the annual cap; the attached letter outlines effects on small owners, deferred maintenance, and reduced supply. We request to present at the hearing.

Linda Hargrove, Director of Government Affairs

Tôi ủng hộ việc giảm mức trần tăng tiền thuê nhà hàng năm. Gia đình tôi thuê căn hộ ở khu Alum Rock và tiền thuê tăng liên tục khiến chúng tôi rất khó khăn. Nhiều gia đình người Việt ở đây cũng vậy. Xin quý vị bỏ phiếu thuận. Cảm ơn quý vị.

Trân trọng,
[name removed]
comments.to_office: Hội đồng Thành phố / City Council

comments.item_title: Apartment Rent Ordinance amendment: annual rent-increase cap
comments.subject: I own ONE rental, please don't lump me with corporations
comments.text: I inherited my parents' duplex and rent one side. I'm not a corporate landlord. I OPPOSE the blanket cap — exempt small owners of a few units, or at least tie it to actual cost increases. Hit the big institutional owners, not families like mine.

comments.item_title: Apartment Rent Ordinance amendment: annual rent-increase cap
comments.subject: yes!! finally
comments.text: SUPPORT. my rent downtown is insane and goes up every year. please pass the lower cap. renters have been ignored forever.

comments.item_title: Apartment Rent Ordinance amendment: annual rent-increase cap
comments.subject: undecided — worried about the number
comments.text: I want to protect tenants but the proposed cap number seems very low. Won't that discourage maintenance and new rentals? Maybe a middle figure tied to inflation. I'm genuinely undecided and hope you find a balanced number.

comments.item_title: Apartment Rent Ordinance amendment: annual rent-increase cap
comments.subject: support + stop the move-in fees loophole
comments.text: I SUPPORT the lower cap but owners already dodge it with huge 'fees' and forced move-outs. Please close those loopholes too, or the cap is meaningless. Yes on a stronger, loophole-free version.

comments.item_title: Apartment Rent Ordinance amendment: annual rent-increase cap
comments.subject: mom-and-pop owner, mixed
comments.text: I own a small place and I sympathize with tenants — I keep my rents low. But a hard cap with no cost pass-through scares me when a roof or water heater fails. I'm torn. Please allow capital-improvement adjustments and I could support it.

comments.item_title: Apartment Rent Ordinance amendment: annual rent-increase cap
comments.subject: my elderly mother can't absorb another increase
comments.text: My mother is 78 and on a fixed income in the same apartment for 30 years. Another big increase will force her out. I SUPPORT the lower cap for seniors especially. Please vote yes.

comments.item_title: Apartment Rent Ordinance amendment: annual rent-increase cap
comments.subject: landlords will just stop renting
comments.text: OPPOSE. Friends who own rentals are already talking about selling or doing short-term instead if the cap drops. You'll shrink the rental pool and make it HARDER to find a place. Classic unintended consequences.

comments.item_title: Proactive rental inspection and habitability enforcement
comments.subject: yes, but I'm scared to put my name
comments.text: I SUPPORT the cap. I'm a renter and honestly scared my landlord retaliates for speaking up, so please keep comments private if you can. We need protection from huge increases AND from retaliation. Thank you.

comments.item_title: Apartment Rent Ordinance amendment: annual rent-increase cap
comments.subject: not sure this is the city's call
comments.text: Isn't rent control mostly a state issue? I'm confused about what the city can even do and whether a local cap survives legally. I don't know if I support it until someone explains what's actually allowed. Please clarify for residents.

comments.item_title: Permitting modernization and fee schedule
comments.subject: against — fix permitting and build instead
comments.text: I OPPOSE the rent cap. The real fix is building more housing — speed up permits and approvals. Price controls treat the symptom. Approve more homes and rents stabilize on their own.

comments.item_title: Apartment Rent Ordinance amendment: annual rent-increase cap
comments.subject: support — I had to move twice already
comments.text: I've been priced out of two apartments in three years, each time further from work. I SUPPORT the lower cap. Stability matters — kids changing schools, longer commutes. Please vote yes.

comments.item_title: Apartment Rent Ordinance amendment: annual rent-increase cap
comments.subject: owner of a fourplex — conditional
comments.text: I own a fourplex near Willow Glen. I'm not against a cap in principle, but it MUST allow pass-through for major repairs and property-tax jumps. With those, I could live with it. Without them I oppose. Please build in fairness for owners too.

comments.item_title: Apartment Rent Ordinance amendment: annual rent-increase cap
comments.subject: Coalition letter in SUPPORT of the rent-cap amendment
comments.text:
Dear Mayor and Honorable Councilmembers,

On behalf of the Sacred Heart Community Housing Alliance and our member organizations, please find attached our formal letter in SUPPORT of lowering the annual rent-increase cap under the Apartment Rent Ordinance.

The attached letter, on our organizational letterhead, summarizes displacement data from East San José and the Mayfair area and includes endorsements from twelve partner groups.

We respectfully urge a YES vote.

Sincerely,
[name removed]
Executive Director
comments.to_office: City Council; Office of the Mayor

comments.item_title: Apartment Rent Ordinance amendment: annual rent-increase cap
comments.subject: eComment: SUPPORT rent cap amendment
comments.text:
eComment — [name removed], renter near Japantown.

I SUPPORT the amendment to lower the annual rent-increase cap. I've rented the same one-bedroom for seven years and the increases every year have pushed me to the edge. Working people are being priced out of the city we grew up in. Please vote yes. (Also submitted by email.)

comments.item_title: Illegal dumping response and Coyote Creek cleanup
comments.subject: illegal dumping Coyote Creek trail
comments.text: There is a huge pile of mattresses and construction debris dumped along the Coyote Creek trail near Kelley Park. Been there weeks. I worry about it getting into the creek. I called 311, got a case number, still there. I SUPPORT the city's creek cleanup — I just need someone to show up this time. Thanks, Lupe

comments.item_title: Illegal dumping response and Coyote Creek cleanup
comments.subject: against cutting the dump cleanup crew
comments.text: I heard the budget may cut the illegal-dumping response team. I OPPOSE that. The Coyote Creek area is already a mess; cutting the crew makes it worse. Keep them funded.

comments.item_title: Illegal dumping response and Coyote Creek cleanup
comments.subject: free dump days would help
comments.text: People dump because legal disposal is expensive and far. I SUPPORT more free bulky-item pickup and dump days. Make it easy to do the right thing and the creek dumping drops. Prevention over cleanup.

comments.item_title: Illegal dumping response and Coyote Creek cleanup
comments.subject: cameras and fines
comments.text: Put cameras at the known dumping spots by the creek and fine people hard. I SUPPORT enforcement. Cleanups without consequences just invite the next dump.

comments.item_title: Illegal dumping response and Coyote Creek cleanup
comments.subject: Basura en el arroyo Coyote
comments.text:
Buenas noches,

Hay mucha basura y escombros tirados cerca del arroyo Coyote, junto al parque Kelley. Lleva semanas y huele mal. Apoyo que la ciudad lo limpie y ponga cámaras para multar a quienes tiran basura. Por favor háganlo pronto. Gracias.

[name removed]

comments.item_title: Illegal dumping response and Coyote Creek cleanup
comments.subject: homeless encampment is the real cause
comments.text: The dumping near the creek is tied to the encampment there. I OPPOSE spending on repeat cleanups without addressing the encampment. Otherwise it's a bottomless pit. Deal with the root cause.

comments.item_title: Illegal dumping response and Coyote Creek cleanup
comments.subject: volunteers ready to help
comments.text: My neighbors and I are happy to do a volunteer cleanup if the city hauls what we gather. I SUPPORT a city-volunteer partnership for the Coyote Creek stretch. Give us gloves and a dumpster and we'll show up.

comments.item_title: Illegal dumping response and Coyote Creek cleanup
comments.subject: not sure whose job this is
comments.text: Is creek dumping a city thing, the water district, or the county? I keep getting transferred. I just want it cleaned near Kelley Park. Not sure what to support, just please someone take it.

comments.item_title: Permitting modernization and fee schedule
comments.subject: ADU permit stuck for 8 months
comments.text: My ADU permit has been 'in review' for EIGHT months. Every cycle they ask for one new thing. I'm trying to build a legal unit for my mother and add housing — the thing the city says it wants. I OPPOSE this broken permitting process. Please fix the backlog.

comments.item_title: Permitting modernization and fee schedule
comments.subject: small business permit nightmare
comments.text: I signed a lease for a café in Willow Glen in January and STILL can't open because of permit and inspection delays. I'm paying rent on an empty space. I OPPOSE how the city treats small businesses. Streamline this or waive my fees for the delay.

comments.item_title: Permitting modernization and fee schedule
comments.subject: Permisos tardan demasiado
comments.text:
Estimados,

Llevo meses esperando el permiso para una pequeña remodelación. Cada vez piden otro documento. Es muy difícil y caro. Me opongo a estos retrasos. Por favor simplifiquen el proceso para la gente común. Gracias.

[name removed]

comments.item_title: Permitting modernization and fee schedule
comments.subject: support the online permitting overhaul
comments.text: I SUPPORT the proposed online permitting modernization. I've lived the paper runaround. Please fund the new system AND hire enough reviewers — software alone won't fix a staffing shortage. Do both.

comments.item_title: Permitting modernization and fee schedule
comments.subject: fees keep going up for worse service
comments.text: Permit fees went UP while wait times got longer. How? I OPPOSE any further fee increase until service improves. Show results, then we'll talk about fees.

comments.item_title: Permitting modernization and fee schedule
comments.subject: solar permit delay
comments.text: My rooftop solar install is done but it's been sitting a month waiting for city permit sign-off while I pay for a system I can't turn on. I support faster clean-energy permitting. This delay discourages exactly what we should encourage.

comments.item_title: Permitting modernization and fee schedule
comments.subject: the counter is understaffed, period
comments.text: I'm a contractor and I'm at the permit counter weekly. It's not corruption, it's understaffing. I'm neutral on the fancy reform plan — just hire more plan checkers. That's the fix. Everything else is window dressing.

comments.item_title: Public safety budget: patrols, community service officers, cameras
comments.subject: car break-ins every week in Naglee Park
comments.text: There have been car break-ins on my Naglee Park block almost weekly. Response times are terrible and reports go nowhere. I OPPOSE the city's current approach. We need visible patrols and someone to actually follow up. People are scared.

comments.item_title: Public safety budget: patrols, community service officers, cameras
comments.subject: support community service officers, not just more police
comments.text: I SUPPORT expanding non-sworn community service officers and better lighting/cameras rather than only adding armed police. Smarter response, not just more of the same. Please fund the alternatives.

comments.item_title: Public safety budget: patrols, community service officers, cameras
comments.subject: Robos en el vecindario
comments.text:
Buenas noches,

En mi vecindario cerca de Story Road ha habido varios robos a autos y casas. Llamamos a la policía y tardan mucho. Me opongo a que nos ignoren. Pedimos más vigilancia y que respondan a tiempo. Gracias por su atención.

[name removed]

comments.item_title: Public safety budget: patrols, community service officers, cameras
comments.subject: stop cutting the police budget
comments.text: Crime is up and you want to cut sworn officers? I OPPOSE any police budget cut. Fund more patrols now. Public safety is the city's first job.

comments.item_title: Public safety budget: patrols, community service officers, cameras
comments.subject: support the youth programs to prevent crime
comments.text: I SUPPORT funding late-night youth programs and job training in East San Jose as crime prevention. Give kids somewhere to be and something to do. Enforcement alone won't fix root causes.

comments.item_title: Public safety budget: patrols, community service officers, cameras
comments.subject: catalytic converter thefts
comments.text: Three catalytic converters stolen on my street this month. I don't know what the right policy is — more patrol? etching programs? I just want the city to do SOMETHING effective. Open to whatever actually works.

comments.item_title: Public safety budget: patrols, community service officers, cameras
comments.subject: against the proposed surveillance cameras
comments.text: I understand the crime worry but I OPPOSE blanketing neighborhoods with city surveillance cameras and license-plate readers. That's a privacy overreach. Fund patrols and lighting, not mass surveillance of residents.

comments.subject: cant find work and about to lose my place
comments.text: i dont know who to write to. i got laid off from a warehouse near monterey rd in april and cant find anything steady. applied to like 60 places. im behind on rent and scared. is there any emergency help the city has?? anything. east san jose

comments.item_title: General correspondence (no agenda item)
comments.subject: medical debt and city help
comments.text: I'm drowning in medical debt and read the county has a relief program but couldn't navigate it. Can the city help connect people to debt relief and financial counseling? I'd support a city navigator program. Feeling lost.

I live near 5th and William downtown. Every rain over an inch the storm drain backs up and water reaches the driveways. Last January it got into my garage. Public Works or Water District? Starting here. Please look before winter. Photo below.

comments.text: everything is too expensive here and nobody in charge seems to care. rent food gas all of it. you keep building for rich people. i dont even know what im asking for anymore. just wanted someone to know people are struggling

comments.item_title: General correspondence (no agenda item)
comments.subject: Phản đối việc đóng cửa trung tâm người cao tuổi
comments.text:
Kính gửi quý vị,

Tôi PHẢN ĐỐI việc cắt giảm giờ của trung tâm người cao tuổi ở khu Alum Rock. Mẹ tôi đến đó mỗi ngày để ăn trưa và gặp bạn bè — nơi duy nhất bà giao tiếp. Nếu cắt giảm, nhiều người già sẽ cô đơn và thiếu bữa ăn. Xin giữ nguyên chương trình. Cảm ơn.

comments.item_title: General correspondence (no agenda item)
comments.subject: air quality near the freeway
comments.text: The air near my place by 101 is visibly hazy and my kid's asthma is worse. I SUPPORT a sound/air wall and more trees along the corridor. Please prioritize freeway-adjacent neighborhoods for air quality help.

comments.item_title: Pavement maintenance: emergency repair on Alma Avenue and road funding
comments.subject: Alma Ave hole — my elderly neighbor fell
comments.text: My elderly neighbor tripped stepping around the Alma Avenue pothole and hurt her wrist. This is beyond cars now — it's a pedestrian hazard too. I OPPOSE any more delay. Please send a crew this week.

comments.item_title: Pavement maintenance: emergency repair on Alma Avenue and road funding
comments.subject: willing to support a street repair levy for roads like Alma
comments.text: The Alma Ave pothole is a symptom — our street budget is too small. I'd SUPPORT a modest dedicated road-repair measure if it's transparent and local. I'm tired of dodging the same crater. Let's fund maintenance properly.

comments.item_title: Pavement maintenance: emergency repair on Alma Avenue and road funding
comments.subject: update on Alma Avenue?
comments.text: Following up — any update on the Alma Ave repair? Neighbors keep asking me. I support the fix; I just need a status. Thanks for any reply.

comments.item_title: Rezoning application: Blossom Hill Road retail parcel
comments.subject: Oppose the Blossom Hill rezoning for the strip mall
comments.text:
Dear Councilmember,

I OPPOSE rezoning the parcel near Blossom Hill Road for another strip mall. We have empty retail already and it'll add traffic to a bad intersection. Please deny the rezoning and consider housing or open space instead.

[name removed]

eComment — [name removed]

I oppose rezoning the Blossom Hill Road parcel for another strip mall — we have vacant retail and this worsens a bad intersection. Deny it; prefer housing or open space. (Same comment I emailed my district office.)
